name: Google Workspace: sign out (and optionally suspend) user
description: Run on a case: signs the case's user out of all Google web and device sessions; if the case is tagged `gws-suspend`, also suspends the account. Writes a note with each HTTP status.

params.label: Admin to impersonate
params.help: Email of the Workspace admin the response service account acts as (domain-wide delegation). Needs user security management and Users > Update (Suspend users) privileges.

secrets.name: GWS_RESPONSE_SA_KEY
secrets.description: Full JSON key of a separate Google Cloud service account used only for containment (Directory API user security + user scopes).

setup:
### Why a separate service account
Pulling alerts needs only `apps.alerts`; containment needs `admin.directory.user`, which can change any user (passwords, admin flags, suspension). Keeping it on its own service account and secret means a leaked pull key cannot sign out or suspend anyone, and you can revoke the containment delegation independently.

### Google Cloud side
1. In a Google Cloud project: APIs & Services > Library > enable **Admin SDK API**.
2. IAM & Admin > Service accounts > **Create service account** (no project roles needed), separate from the alert reader. Keys > Add key > **JSON**.
3. Copy its **OAuth 2 Client ID** (numeric) from the Details page.

### Admin console side (super admin)
1. Security > Access and data control > API controls > **Manage Domain Wide Delegation** > Add new: the client ID, OAuth scopes `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user.security,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user`, Authorize (up to 24 h to apply). If you never suspend, authorise only the first scope: each call asks only for its own scope.
2. Pick the admin to impersonate (`ADMIN_EMAIL`): a Super Admin, or (least privilege) a custom role with **Users: Read** and **Users: Update > Suspend users**, and **Security > User Security Management** (sign-in cookie reset). A delegated admin cannot act on users above their own role (e.g. super admins).

### Here
1. Settings > Secrets: add `GWS_RESPONSE_SA_KEY` with the whole JSON key file, allowed hosts `oauth2.googleapis.com` **and** `admin.googleapis.com`.
2. Install with `ADMIN_EMAIL`.

### What it does
Target = the case's `username` attribute, else its first `email` artifact, used as the Google `userKey` (primary or alias email). With no target it only writes a note.
1. `POST https://admin.googleapis.com/admin/directory/v1/users/<email>/signOut` (scope `admin.directory.user.security`; empty body, 2xx = done): ends the user's web and device sessions and resets sign-in cookies. It does not change the password, so pair it with a password reset when credentials are compromised.
2. Only if the case has the tag `gws-suspend`: `PUT https://admin.googleapis.com/admin/directory/v1/users/<email>` with `{"suspended": true}` (scope `admin.directory.user`; `update` keeps fields that are not sent, and Google recommends it over `patch`). Un-suspend by sending `false` or in the Admin console.
3. Note with both HTTP statuses.

Docs: [users.signOut](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/reference/rest/v1/users/signOut), [users.update](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/reference/rest/v1/users/update), [Domain-wide delegation](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/v1/guides/delegation), [Sign a user out](https://support.google.com/a/answer/178854).

## Containment guardrails
A **containment guard** step runs before the action: targets protected in **Settings → Integrations → Containment guardrails** (VIPs, domain controllers, critical ranges) are never contained automatically, and the tenant's daily and per-case caps apply. A refusal stops the run and adds a case note; every action is listed on the case under **Artifacts & assets → Containment**, where an analyst marks it released once undone.
